runs.t: Laser Toning
1. Hero & Intro
Laser Toning Treatment

Living in a city as sunny as Delhi, most of us carry some sun damage whether we notice it or not. It shows up as dark spots on the cheeks, a patchy forehead, or skin that just doesn't look as even as it used to. Creams can lighten the surface a little, but the pigment that causes these marks often sits deeper. That's what a laser toning treatment in Delhi is meant to reach.

Laser toning uses gentle laser light to break up that deeper pigment without harming the top layer of skin. Your body clears the broken pigment over the following weeks, and tone gradually evens out. The heat also nudges the skin to make fresh collagen, which can help with texture and glow. There's no numbing, no downtime, and you can go straight back to work.
Available at Dadu Medical Centre Vasant Vihar (South Delhi) & Rajouri Garden (West Delhi), under Dr. Nivedita Dadu.
2. How Laser Toning Works

Laser toning uses a non-ablative laser, which means it works under the skin's surface without peeling or wounding it. The light is set to a wavelength that pigment absorbs. As it reaches the deeper layers, it breaks the clusters of pigment behind dark spots and uneven tone into tiny fragments, which your body then clears away over the next days and weeks.

There's a second effect too. The gentle heat from the laser reaches the dermis and encourages new collagen. Over a course of sessions, that can make skin feel a little firmer and look smoother and brighter, on top of the lighter pigmentation.
3. What Laser Toning Can Help With

The main reason people book it is sun-related pigmentation: dark spots, patchy areas and that general unevenness that builds up over years outdoors. It's also used for dull skin and early photoageing, and the collagen boost can help with texture and firmness along the way.

Uneven pigmentation is partly a normal part of ageing, and our climate certainly doesn't help. Laser toning can make a visible difference, but it works gradually, and how far the marks fade depends on how deep and how old they are.

5. Ideal Candidates

It suits people with sun spots, patchy pigmentation or skin that's lost its evenness over time. Those noticing early signs of sun damage, or who simply want their complexion to look clearer and more uniform, are also good candidates. It can be used on a range of skin types, though your doctor will check your skin first and adjust the approach.
6. Process & Techniques

A doctor first examines your skin and the pigmentation to decide whether laser toning is right for you and how many sessions to plan. Usually no priming or special preparation is needed, though your doctor may give you specific instructions.
During the session, the laser is passed over the face. Most people feel only slight warmth, and anaesthetic isn't normally needed. Once it's done, you can go straight back to your routine.
How many sessions?

That depends on your skin type and how much sun damage there is. Some people see a change after three or four sessions, while deeper or older pigmentation needs more. Results build gradually over the full course and vary from person to person.

Aftercare:

Sunscreen is non-negotiable. Your skin is more sensitive to UV after each session, and without proper sun protection pigmentation can come back or even get darker. Apply it daily and reapply when you're outdoors.

9. FAQs
Q: What is laser toning?
Ans. A non-invasive laser treatment that breaks up pigment under the skin's surface to fade dark spots and even out skin tone.
Q: Does laser toning hurt?
Ans. Usually not. You may feel some warmth, and numbing cream generally isn't needed.
Q: How many sessions will I need?
Ans. It depends on your skin type and how severe the pigmentation is. Some people see results after three or four sessions; others need more.
Q: Is there downtime?
Ans. No. You can go back to your normal routine right after the session.
Q: Why is sunscreen so important afterwards?
Ans. Treated skin is more sensitive to UV. Without sunscreen, pigmentation can return or get worse.
Q: Does it help with sun damage?
Ans. Yes. It's particularly useful for sun-induced spots, patchiness and uneven tone.
Q: Can it improve skin texture?
Ans. It can. The laser's heat encourages collagen, which helps texture and firmness over time.
Q: Is laser toning suitable for all skin types?
Ans. It can be used on many skin types, but a doctor needs to assess your skin first and adjust the settings.
